Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA Automation Engineer with 7 years of experience, including 2+ years focused on CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral test environments and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and has improved pipeline speed, environment availability and test reliability. Builds test environments with Docker and Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster, and has personal hands-on experience with k3s, GitOps, observability and Terraform. Transitioning toward a DevOps / platform infrastructure role.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level access; test environments), k3s, Argo CD
Infrastructure as Code & Automation: Terraform (personal project), Ansible (basic), Bash, Python
Observability & Data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL, SQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Systems & Cloud: Linux, AWS (EC2 and S3 basics; personal learning)
Other: Git, Java (test code)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software | Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, as well as artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes by profiling workflows, parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests; monthly CI runner costs decreased by approximately 30%.
- Built per-merge-request ephemeral test environments using Docker Compose and later Helm charts on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster; environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, and are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Built a Python and PostgreSQL test-results pipeline and Grafana dashboards to help teams identify flaky tests.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding and authored an internal guide to CI used in team onboarding.
- Mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House | Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform.
- Technologies: k3s, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Terraform, Ansible (basic).

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation | Exam scheduled for January 2027

LANGUAGES
Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible and well-structured CV. It presents clear progression from QA automation into test infrastructure and DevOps-adjacent work, with quantified outcomes such as reducing pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes, reducing runner costs by approximately 30%, and lowering flaky tests below 1%. The experience bullets are specific, technically credible and professionally written. The document also handles seniority and scope honestly by clarifying namespace-level Kubernetes access, personal Terraform work and AWS basics. The main content limitation is that the CV is stronger for CI/CD and test infrastructure than for cloud infrastructure engineering, systems design and networking.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional headings, chronological experience, searchable technology names and simple text formatting without tables, graphics or unusual section labels. Important keywords including Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, GitLab CI, AWS, Linux, Prometheus, Grafana, TLS and infrastructure are present. AI screening probability is moderate to good for junior or transitional DevOps/platform roles, but lower for this specific contractor role because the CV does not show Terragrunt, mTLS, substantial AWS infrastructure, cloud environment operation, systems architecture or virtual machines. The explicit qualifiers such as “personal project,” “basic,” and “namespace-level access” improve truthfulness but also correctly signal limited depth to automated screening.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows relevant hands-on infrastructure work through GitLab CI ownership, ephemeral environments, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, observability and a personal k3s/GitOps platform. It also demonstrates analytical thinking, technical ownership and clear communication through measurable pipeline improvements, the internal CI guide and mentoring. However, the candidate's material does not support strong Terraform/Terragrunt experience, mTLS, production cloud operations, IoT or remote-device integration, or virtual-machine experience. AWS exposure is limited to personal learning with EC2 and S3 basics. The closest alignment is therefore with a junior-to-mid DevOps or platform infrastructure position rather than the full scope of this cloud infrastructure contractor role. The CV does not currently demonstrate leading cross-team architecture proposals, negotiating interfaces with external stakeholders, or designing secure train-to-cloud communications.
critique.improvement_instructions:
Minor, targeted enhancements only:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace “Transitioning toward a DevOps / platform infrastructure role” with a more evidence-led statement such as: “QA Automation Engineer transitioning into DevOps and platform infrastructure, with hands-on ownership of CI/CD, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, GitOps observability and infrastructure automation.” This better matches the ad without overstating production cloud experience.
2. In the Odrava Health Software experience section, revise the ephemeral-environment bullet to include the collaboration outcome already supported by the candidate portfolio: “Built per-merge-request ephemeral test environments using Docker Compose and Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster, enabling QA and product teams to review features before merge; environments included the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data and were automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.”
3. In the same Odrava section, strengthen the internal-documentation bullet using the original candidate information: change “authored an internal guide to CI used in team onboarding” to “authored the internal ‘How Our CI Works’ guide, now used in team onboarding.” This makes communication and technical knowledge sharing more visible.
4. In the Selected Infrastructure Project section, clarify the security/networking scope without implying mTLS: change “cert-manager for TLS” to “Traefik ingress with cert-manager-managed TLS certificates.” This is more precise and improves keyword relevance for TLS and certificate management.
5. In the Technical Skills section, retain the qualification labels but make the personal scope consistently explicit by changing “Terraform (personal project)” to “Terraform (personal Hetzner project)” and “AWS (EC2 and S3 basics; personal learning)” to “AWS: EC2 and S3 basics (personal learning).” This prevents recruiters from interpreting these as professional cloud infrastructure experience while preserving relevant ATS keywords.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, professional, and strongly quantified. The main content weakness is role alignment: the CV demonstrates CI/test infrastructure more strongly than cloud infrastructure engineering, systems architecture, networking, security, or production platform operation. The summary is also somewhat repetitive, stating the transition into DevOps/platform infrastructure twice.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, readable text formatting, and relevant keywords such as Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, GitLab CI, Linux, AWS, Prometheus, Grafana, TLS, and Argo CD. Parsing compatibility should be good. AI screening probability for this specific role is moderate rather than high because important job terms are absent or weakly represented: Terragrunt, systems architecture, system design, networking, mTLS, certificate management, security awareness, cloud environment operation, and stakeholder engagement. critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a good adjacent match for hands-on infrastructure engineering through Docker, Helm, Kubernetes test environments, GitLab CI, observability, and the personal k3s/Terraform project. It also shows strong analytical thinking and communication through pipeline profiling, measurable optimisation, documentation, onboarding use, and dashboards. It has some evidence of leading technical topics and engaging stakeholders through ownership for three product teams and enabling QA/product review environments. However, the candidate material indicates meaningful gaps for this contractor role: Terraform is limited to a personal Hetzner project, Terragrunt is not present, systems architecture and system-design experience are not established, and there is no stated mTLS, networking, practical security, IoT/automotive, remote-device, or backend/full-stack experience. AWS is only at basic personal-learning level. Linux is shown, but virtual-machine experience is not. The role therefore appears to be a developing or adjacent match rather than a strong direct match for a contractor expected to shape production fleet-connectivity infrastructure.

Its ownership, collaboration, observability, and continuous-improvement evidence aligns positively with the company's engineering-led and collaborative culture.
